BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Weak layers in the old snowpack necessitate caution. Fresh wind slabs require caution.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
Weak layers in the lower part of the snowpack can be released by winter sport participants. This applies on steep west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Remotely triggered avalanches are possible in isolated cases. This applies in high Alpine regions. Mostly the avalanches are medium-sized.
In addition the fresh wind slabs should be taken into account. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised adjacent to ridgelines, as well as in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase with altitude. Avalanches can reach medium size.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment:
Avalanche prone weak layers exist in the old snowpack. This applies in particular on west, north and east facing slopes above approximately 2600 m, as well as in all aspects above approximately 3000 m. Whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack and fresh avalanches serve as an alarm indicating the danger.

Over a wide area 15 to 20 cm of snow, and up to 30 cm in some localities, fell on Thursday. The wind has transported the new snow. This applies in particular at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions. The fresh wind slabs are lying on soft layers.
BulletinMeasurements.tendencyComment: The avalanche danger will persist. Experience in the assessment of avalanche danger is required.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Wind slabs require caution. Slab avalanches are possible.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The wind slabs can still be released in some cases, in particular on very steep slopes. Backcountry tourers can release avalanches in some places, including medium-sized ones.
On extreme sunny slopes and in steep rocky terrain small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized natural loose snow slides are to be expected as a consequence of warming during the day and solar radiation.
Gliding avalanches can also occur, in particular on steep grassy slopes. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment:
In particular in the northwest 15 to 30 cm of snow fell in the last few days above approximately 1300 m.
As a consequence of the occasionally strong northerly wind, the snow drift accumulations have increased in size during the last few days.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 70 to 140 cm of snow, and even as much as 180 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
During the sunny day, the surface snow becomes moist below 2500 m. In some places, where the wind has had a greater effect, it has a chalky consistency.
It is not distinctly layered. Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2300 m.
BulletinMeasurements.tendencyComment: The weather conditions will facilitate a gradual strengthening of the snowpack.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Fresh and older wind slabs are to be assessed with care and prudence.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The sometimes strong wind has transported the new snow significantly. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls the wind slabs have increased in size additionally.
New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. Above approximately 2300 m the avalanches can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size. This applies in particular at transitions from a shallow to a deep snowpack.
In particular in steep rocky terrain small and medium-sized moist avalanches are possible as a consequence of solar radiation.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
BulletinMeasurements.snowpackStructureComment: 30 to 50 cm of snow has fallen since Tuesday above approximately 1500 m. The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind. This applies especially at high altitudes and in high Alpine regions.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Fresh wind slabs require caution. Weak layers in the old snowpack necessitate caution.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The fresh wind slabs represent the main danger. Such avalanche prone locations are to be found in steep terrain above approximately 2400 m. Caution is to be exercised adjacent to ridgelines, as well as in gullies and bowls, and behind abrupt changes in the terrain. The number and size of avalanche prone locations will increase with altitude. In regions with a lot of snow the avalanche prone locations are more prevalent and the danger is slightly greater. Avalanches can reach medium size.

The wind slabs of the last few days can still be released in some cases, in particular on very steep slopes. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls and behind abrupt changes in the terrain the likelihood of avalanches is higher.
As the day progresses the likelihood of dry and moist snow slides being released will increase on extremely steep sunny slopes. Mostly these are small.

In addition the wind slabs are capable of being triggered in some locations. This applies in particular on very steep slopes.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Wind slabs represent the main danger.

Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher. The prevalence of avalanche prone locations and likelihood of triggering will increase with altitude.

BulletinMeasurements.avActivityHighlights: Individual avalanche prone locations are to be found at high altitude.
BulletinMeasurements.avActivityComment:
The avalanche prone locations are very rare. They are to be found on extremely steep shady slopes at elevated altitudes and on wind-loaded slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation individual small natural moist avalanches are possible. Restraint should be exercised because avalanches can sweep people along and give rise to falls.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.
